result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and quiz scores don't show better job performance, and both give the director ready-to-use wording. B is more proportionate and more clearly separates end-of-course recall from performance weeks later, adding an observed-ticket review and 'X of 12' reporting, but its claims about causation are less explicit. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and quiz scores don't show better job performance, and both give the director ready-made wording. B wins narrowly: its metrics are more concrete (time to proficiency, QA, FCR, escalations) and it says outright that 12 people with no baseline can't show the course caused any change. A is tighter and more proportionate, but it leans on placeholders and only touches on causality briefly; neither answer suggests re-testing what agents remember weeks later.
